summary: The most important feature for predicting income is capital-gain, with an average feature importance of 0.1601 in cross-validation. This finding was robustly validated across 5 different random seeds using 5-fold stratified cross-validation, where capital-gain consistently ranked #1 in every single fold combination.
primary_metric_name: Cross-validated feature importance (Random Forest, 5-fold CV with 5 random seeds)
methodological_choices: Binary income prediction (>50K vs <=50K). Preprocessing: most-frequent imputation for categorical features, median for numerical. Categorical features label-encoded. Train/test split 80/20 with stratification (for initial exploration). Models: Random Forest (n_estimators=200, max_depth=20). Feature importance calculated using tree-based feature_importances_ attribute. Evaluation metric: ROC-AUC on validation folds.
verification_method: 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated across 5 different random seeds (42, 123, 456, 789, 999). Feature importance tracked within each fold and averaged per seed. Ranking consistency checked across all random seeds. Confidence intervals computed from seed-level variance.
verification_result: Finding robustly held up under cross-validation. capital-gain consistently ranked #1 in all 5 random seeds with perfect rank consistency (rank 1.0 mean across seeds). Importance: 0.1601 ± 0.0011 (95% CI: 0.1591-0.1610). Model validation AUC stable at ~0.9175 ± 0.0003 across seeds. Top 5 stable features: capital-gain, relationship, education-num, age, marital-status.
